show_file <- function(path, n = Inf) {
  x <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  if (is.finite(n)) x <- head(x, n)
  cat(paste(x, collapse = "\n"))
}

show_source_block <- function(path, lang = "text") {
  x <- paste(readLines(path, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
  cat(sprintf("<pre><code class=\"language-%s\">", lang))
  cat(htmltools::htmlEscape(x))
  cat("</code></pre>")
}

file_table <- function(paths) {
  info <- file.info(paths)
  data.frame(
    file = paths,
    exists = file.exists(paths),
    size_mb = round(info$size / 1024^2, 3),
    modified = as.character(info$mtime),
    row.names = NULL
  )
}
```

# Purpose

This RMarkdown documents the complete workflow used to obtain:

`r final_report`

The workflow starts from a Xenium `SpatialFeatureExperiment` object and an IMC `SingleCellExperiment` object, transfers fibroblast and endothelial metabolic annotations into the Xenium data, trains MintFlow, performs in silico perturbations of `Met_hi_Fib`, and generates the final EC-response report with frequency-colored dot plots and high-resolution tissue maps.

By default, this document renders in audit mode. It checks existing inputs/outputs and prints all reproducibility commands, but it does not rerun the computationally heavy MintFlow training or generation steps. To rerun heavy steps during rendering, render with `params = list(run_heavy = TRUE)`. To also rerun the final lightweight report/plot post-processing chunks during rendering, use `params = list(run_render_steps = TRUE)`.

# Software Environment

MintFlow was run from the Python virtual environment at `/tmp/mintflow_venv`. The R conversion step requires Bioconductor classes for spatial single-cell objects. The exact environment can be checked with:

```{bash check-env, eval=FALSE}
python - <<'PY'
import sys
print(sys.executable)
for pkg in ["anndata", "scanpy", "squidpy", "mintflow", "torch", "sklearn", "pandas", "numpy", "matplotlib", "seaborn"]:
    try:
        mod = __import__(pkg)
        print(pkg, getattr(mod, "__version__", "version not exposed"))
    except Exception as exc:
        print(pkg, "NOT AVAILABLE", exc)
PY

Rscript -e 'pkgs <- c("SpatialFeatureExperiment","SingleCellExperiment","SummarizedExperiment","Matrix","rmarkdown","knitr"); print(setNames(pkgs %in% rownames(installed.packages()), pkgs)); sessionInfo()'
```

The local requirements snapshot used while creating the MintFlow environment is:

```{r requirements, results='asis'}
req <- file.path(workdir, "requirements_mintflow_tmp_env.txt")
if (file.exists(req)) {
  cat("```text\n")
  cat(paste(readLines(req, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"))
  cat("\n```\n")
} else {
  cat("No requirements snapshot found at ", req, "\n")
}
```

# Step 1: Export the SFE and Transfer IMC-Derived Labels

This step reads the Xenium SFE and the IMC SPE. It transfers metabolic fibroblast and endothelial annotations from the IMC object to Xenium using `KEY`:

`Met_hi_Fib`: IMC `Rphenograph_500` clusters `1` or `2`

`Other_Fib`: IMC `Rphenograph_500` cluster `3`

`Met_hi_EC`: IMC `Rphenograph_200EC` clusters `1` or `2`

`Met_int_EC`: IMC `Rphenograph_200EC` cluster `3`

The combined label used for MintFlow is `combined_met_label`, prioritizing fibroblast labels if a cell has both fibroblast and EC labels. The script writes a Matrix Market bundle to `anndata_bundle_combined_fib_ec`:

`counts_genes_by_cells.mtx`: sparse count matrix, genes by cells

`obs.csv`: cell metadata including transferred labels, coordinates, sample, and annotation columns

`var.csv`: gene metadata

```{bash export-sfe, eval=params$run_heavy}
Rscript inputs/mintflow/export_sfe_for_anndata_combined_fib_ec.R \
  "inputs/Revision/Nan annotation/Data/Xenium sfe objects/Xenium sfe object/sfe_09032026.rds" \
  "inputs/Revision/Nan annotation/Data/IMC spe objects/New IMC/spe2025-12-17 umap.RData" \
  inputs/mintflow/anndata_bundle_combined_fib_ec
```

```{r export-bundle-check}
bundle_files <- file.path(bundle_dir, c("counts_genes_by_cells.mtx", "obs.csv", "var.csv"))
file_table(bundle_files)

if (file.exists(file.path(bundle_dir, "obs.csv"))) {
  obs <- read.csv(file.path(bundle_dir, "obs.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
  print(table(obs$combined_met_label, useNA = "ifany"))
  print(table(obs$metfiblabel, useNA = "ifany"))
  print(table(obs$metEClabel, useNA = "ifany"))
}
```

# Step 2: Convert the Export Bundle to AnnData

MintFlow expects AnnData input. The Python conversion script reads the Matrix Market bundle, transposes the count matrix to cells by genes, keeps the relevant metadata, stores Xenium centroids as `obsm["spatial"]`, and writes:

`inputs/mintflow/xenium_sfe_09032026_combined_fib_ec_metlabel.h5ad`

```{bash make-h5ad, eval=params$run_heavy}
python inputs/mintflow/make_h5ad_from_export.py \
  --bundle-dir inputs/mintflow/anndata_bundle_combined_fib_ec \
  --out inputs/mintflow/xenium_sfe_09032026_combined_fib_ec_metlabel.h5ad
```

```{bash inspect-h5ad, eval=FALSE}
python - <<'PY'
import anndata as ad
adata = ad.read_h5ad("inputs/mintflow/xenium_sfe_09032026_combined_fib_ec_metlabel.h5ad")
print(adata)
print(adata.obs["combined_met_label"].value_counts(dropna=False))
print(adata.obs[["cell_id","sample_id","combined_met_label","metfiblabel","metEClabel","x_centroid","y_centroid"]].head())
PY
```

# Step 3: Train MintFlow

The model was trained using `combined_met_label` as the cell-type label, so MintFlow learned a spatial generative model with these four relevant metabolic cell states:

`Met_hi_Fib`, `Other_Fib`, `Met_hi_EC`, `Met_int_EC`

Training outputs were written to:

`inputs/mintflow/outputs_combined_fib_ec`

The training script saves predictions, optional evaluation files, epoch checkpoints, and the final checkpoint:

`checkpoint_final.pt`

```{bash train-mintflow, eval=params$run_heavy}
python inputs/mintflow/train_mintflow_xenium.py \
  --h5ad inputs/mintflow/xenium_sfe_09032026_combined_fib_ec_metlabel.h5ad \
  --outdir inputs/mintflow/outputs_combined_fib_ec \
  --obskey-cell-type combined_met_label \
  --epochs 20 \
  --width-window 100
```

```{r training-output-check}
train_files <- list.files(file.path(workdir, "outputs_combined_fib_ec"), full.names = TRUE)
file_table(train_files)
```

# Step 4: MintFlow In Silico Perturbation

The perturbation analysis used the trained checkpoint and created three versions of the same tissue:

`baseline`: the original Xenium AnnData with all labels unchanged

`remove_Met_hi_Fib`: all `Met_hi_Fib` cells removed before generating expression

`replace_Met_hi_Fib_with_Other_Fib`: all `Met_hi_Fib` cells relabeled to `Other_Fib` before generating expression

For each scenario, the script recomputes a spatial neighbor graph and calls `mintflow.generate_insilico_ST_data` using the trained model. Five generated realizations are averaged through the `MintFLow_Generated_Xmic` arrays.

The command below is the command encoded in the original report. `--reuse-generations` means the large generation pickles are reused when present instead of regenerated:

```{bash perturb-analysis, eval=params$run_heavy}
python inputs/mintflow/perturb_met_hi_fib_ec_analysis.py \
  --h5ad inputs/mintflow/xenium_sfe_09032026_combined_fib_ec_metlabel.h5ad \
  --checkpoint inputs/mintflow/outputs_combined_fib_ec/checkpoint_final.pt \
  --outdir inputs/mintflow/perturb_met_hi_fib_ec \
  --num-realisations 5 \
  --n-neighs 5 \
  --reuse-generations
```

Main intermediate files saved by this step:

`generation_baseline.pkl`: MintFlow generated baseline realizations and MCC arrays

`generation_remove_Met_hi_Fib.pkl`: MintFlow generated perturbation with `Met_hi_Fib` removed

`generation_replace_Met_hi_Fib_with_Other_Fib.pkl`: MintFlow generated perturbation with `Met_hi_Fib` replaced by `Other_Fib`

`ec_cell_level_perturbation_results.csv`: one row per EC per scenario, with predicted EC state, probability, generated scores, and MCC-change flag

`ec_state_frequency_among_all_ecs.csv`: EC-state frequencies used for the main frequency plots

`ec_summary_perturbation_results.csv`: per original EC label summary

`ec_sample_level_perturbation_results.csv`: per sample and original EC label summary

`ec_classifier_report.json`: logistic-regression classifier performance on baseline generated EC expression

`score_genes_used.json`: Xenium genes used in generated-expression score calculations

```{r perturb-output-check}
perturb_files <- list.files(base_perturb_dir, full.names = TRUE)
file_table(perturb_files)
```

## EC Classifier and Frequency Logic

MintFlow keeps the supplied cell-type labels fixed during generation. To estimate whether generated EC expression resembles `Met_hi_EC` or `Met_int_EC`, the analysis trains a logistic regression classifier on baseline generated EC expression using the original transferred `metEClabel`. The classifier is then applied to generated EC expression in each perturbation scenario.

The main frequency table reports predicted EC-state composition among all ECs. This is why baseline is approximately `52.5% Met_hi_EC` and `47.5% Met_int_EC`, rather than a forced `100% / 0%` split.

```{r ec-frequency-table}
freq <- read.csv(file.path(final_dir, "ec_state_frequency_among_all_ecs.csv"))
freq
```

```{r classifier-report}
jsonlite_available <- requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)
if (jsonlite_available) {
  jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(final_dir, "ec_classifier_report.json"))
} else {
  cat(readLines(file.path(final_dir, "ec_classifier_report.json")), sep = "\n")
}
```

# Step 5: Add Frequency-Colored Dot Plots and Write the Final HTML

The original perturbation report contained bar plots. The final report folder was generated by copying the non-generation outputs from `perturb_met_hi_fib_ec` to `perturb_met_hi_fib_ec_with_frequency_dotplots`, then adding a matrix-style dot plot where dot color encodes EC-state frequency.

This script writes:

`ec_state_frequency_among_all_ecs_pairwise_dotplot.pdf`

`ec_state_frequency_among_all_ecs_pairwise_dotplot.png`

`mintflow_met_hi_fib_perturbation_ec_report_with_frequency_dotplots.html`

```{bash frequency-dotplot-report, eval=params$run_render_steps}
python inputs/mintflow/make_perturb_report_with_frequency_dotplots.py
```

```{r final-report-check}
file_table(c(
  final_report,
  file.path(final_dir, "ec_state_frequency_among_all_ecs_pairwise_dotplot.pdf"),
  file.path(final_dir, "ec_state_frequency_among_all_ecs_pairwise_dotplot.png")
))
```

```{r show-dotplot, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(final_dir, "ec_state_frequency_among_all_ecs_pairwise_dotplot.png"))
```

# Step 6: Generate High-Resolution Tissue Map Exports

The final folder also contains larger tissue-map exports for cropping. These maps are regenerated from the original H5AD plus `ec_cell_level_perturbation_results.csv`, not from a new MintFlow generation. The script reconstructs the three scenario tissues and merges EC probabilities from the saved cell-level table.

The script writes both PDF and 600 DPI PNG outputs:

`tissue_maps_celltype_perturbations_highres.pdf/png`

`tissue_maps_ec_met_hi_probability_highres.pdf/png`

`tissue_maps_met_hi_ec_met_hi_probability_highres.pdf/png`

`tissue_maps_met_int_ec_met_hi_probability_highres.pdf/png`

```{bash highres-maps, eval=params$run_render_steps}
python inputs/mintflow/make_highres_tissue_maps_for_dotplot_report.py
```

```{r highres-check}
highres_files <- list.files(final_dir, pattern = "highres\\.(pdf|png)$", full.names = TRUE)
file_table(highres_files)
```

# Reproducibility Commands as One Shell Script

The commands below reproduce the workflow from exported labels through the final report. Remove `--reuse-generations` if the MintFlow in silico perturbations should be regenerated from scratch.

```{bash full-workflow-script, eval=FALSE}
set -euo pipefail

WORKDIR="inputs/mintflow"
PY="python"
SFE="inputs/Revision/Nan annotation/Data/Xenium sfe objects/Xenium sfe object/sfe_09032026.rds"
SPE="inputs/Revision/Nan annotation/Data/IMC spe objects/New IMC/spe2025-12-17 umap.RData"

Rscript "$WORKDIR/export_sfe_for_anndata_combined_fib_ec.R" \
  "$SFE" \
  "$SPE" \
  "$WORKDIR/anndata_bundle_combined_fib_ec"

"$PY" "$WORKDIR/make_h5ad_from_export.py" \
  --bundle-dir "$WORKDIR/anndata_bundle_combined_fib_ec" \
  --out "$WORKDIR/xenium_sfe_09032026_combined_fib_ec_metlabel.h5ad"

"$PY" "$WORKDIR/train_mintflow_xenium.py" \
  --h5ad "$WORKDIR/xenium_sfe_09032026_combined_fib_ec_metlabel.h5ad" \
  --outdir "$WORKDIR/outputs_combined_fib_ec" \
  --obskey-cell-type combined_met_label \
  --epochs 20 \
  --width-window 100

"$PY" "$WORKDIR/perturb_met_hi_fib_ec_analysis.py" \
  --h5ad "$WORKDIR/xenium_sfe_09032026_combined_fib_ec_metlabel.h5ad" \
  --checkpoint "$WORKDIR/outputs_combined_fib_ec/checkpoint_final.pt" \
  --outdir "$WORKDIR/perturb_met_hi_fib_ec" \
  --num-realisations 5 \
  --n-neighs 5 \
  --reuse-generations

"$PY" "$WORKDIR/make_perturb_report_with_frequency_dotplots.py"
"$PY" "$WORKDIR/make_highres_tissue_maps_for_dotplot_report.py"
```
